_comment: ARABIC template (Egyptian + Levantine MIX — never labelled on screen). The answer is shown as TRANSLITERATION in Latin letters (green — the phonetics), with the native ARABIC SCRIPT on a smaller line BELOW it. Per item: prompt = English shown phrase, answer = transliteration revealed in green (keep ≤13 chars so it stays ONE line), native = Arabic script shown beneath. The spoken voiceover reads the native Arabic. Middle-Eastern character, ROW of flags (eg/lb/jo/sy/ps) to signal 'many dialects', voice salma (default Arabic Levantine female) + model eleven_multilingual_v2. ARABIC IS RTL — Chromium's bidi handles direction inside an Arabic run automatically; we bundle Cairo.ttf so glyphs JOIN and never tofu (listed in fonts[], copied to public/fonts/ by build.sh, appended to the font stack by src/font.ts). Keep to ~7 items so the two-line answers don't crowd. Backgrounds: set an Arab-world bg_query per video; a Pexels miss falls back to the curated versatile-arabic pool (so it never pulls a wrong-region image). Pick whichever everyday spoken form (Egyptian or Levantine) is most natural per word and let viewers argue in the comments.
outro: Follow me to learn Arabic every day
